shortDescription: Indonesia's stock exchange IDX has adopted more market reforms, such as widening the scope of its list of companies with high concentration of shareholdings and changing IPO rules ahead of a key review by index provider MSCI next month.

children: Indonesia's stock exchange IDX has adopted more market reforms, such as widening the scope of its list of companies with high concentration of shareholdings and changing IPO rules ahead of a key review by index provider MSCI next month.

The updated list halves to 5 trillion rupiah ($280 million), the market value threshold for firms with concentrated ownership, aiming to make comprehensive information available to investors, the exchange said in a statement
The exchange now also identifies in its data if an investor is based domestically or offshore, it said

For IPOs, the IDX has scrapped a minimum share price requirement of 100 rupiah to make shares more affordable and  fundraising easier, in line with an earlier removal of a minimum price for traded shares

The exchange allowed a company set to launch an IPO to ask the IDX to count shareholders with a stake of more than 5% in free floats, so long as the beneficiary is a public investor that meets criteria
Indonesia's stock market reforms followed an MSCI warning in January of possible downgrade to "frontier" from "emerging" market status, over transparency concerns.
In June, MSCI extended its review and warned it could consider a downgrade if it judged progress insufficient by the time of the November review.
